title: We let an AI agent edit a Tesseract model's weights directly; it beat a last-layer refit, not fine-tuning

posts.cooked:
e tried weight-space programming (Takehi, Teoh, Zhang & Khattab, MIT CSAIL) on a small production model: Tesseract’s Hebrew text recognizer, 378K weights.

An AI agent (Claude Opus 5.5) edited the weights directly, with no gradients, three times:

  • modern Hebrew text errors 4.18% → 2.64% on average (2.29% best);
  • better than retraining the output layer (3.31%);
  • worse than a full fine-tune on the same 2,000 lines (1.77%).

The fixes were explainable: the agent found two start-up faults in the bidirectional LSTM, one of which swallowed numbers at the start of a Hebrew line.

Fine-tuning won this round, but we still find the result impressive: with no gradients and no training loop, an agent cut the errors by more than a third and could explain every change it made. This was a small model, and larger ones may behave differently. As agents get better, we believe weight-space editing will become a far more valuable tool.

Write-up with the negative results: Weight-Space Programming: An AI Agent vs Fine-Tuning — Rivok Labs
The fine-tuned Hebrew models we ship: Rivok/tesseract-heb-rivok · Hugging Face

Happy to answer questions about the setup.
